source_text: Ἀνάστασίς ἐστι τοῦ πεπτωκότος σαρκίου· πνεῦμα γὰρ οὐ πίπτει. Ψυχὴ ἐν σώματί ἐστιν, οὐ ζῇ δὲ ἄψυχον· σῶμα, ψυχῆς ἀπολειπούσης, οὐκ ἔστιν. Oἶκος γὰρ τὸ σῶμα ψυχῆς, πνεύματος δὲ ψυχὴ οἶκος. Τὰ τρία δὲ ταῦτα τοῖς ἐλπίδα εἰλικρινῆ καὶ πίστιν ἀδιάκριτον ἐν τῷ θεῷ ἔχουσι σωθήσεται. Θεωροῦντες γοῦν καὶ τοὺς κοσμικοὺς λόγους, καὶ κατ' αὐτοὺς οὐχ εὑρίσκοντες ἀδύνατον ὑπάρχειν τῇ σαρκὶ τὴν παλιγγενεσίαν, καὶ ἐπὶ τούτοις πᾶσι τὸν σωτῆρα διὰ παντὸς τοῦ εὐαγγελίου δεικνύντα τὴν τῆς σαρκὸς ἡμῶν σωτηρίαν, τί λοιπὸν ἀνεχόμεθα τῶν ἀπίστων καὶ σκανδάλων λόγων, καὶ λανθάνομεν ἑαυτοὺς ἐπιστρέφοντες εἰς τοὐπίσω, ὁπόταν ἀκούσωμεν ὅτι ἡ μὲν ψυχὴ ἀθάνατός ἐστι, τὸ δὲ σῶμα φθαρτὸν καὶ οὐκέτι δυνάμενον ἀναζῆσαι; Ταῦτα γὰρ καὶ πρὸ τοῦ μαθεῖν τὴν ἀλήθειαν παρὰ Πυθαγόρου καὶ Πλάτωνος ἠκούομεν. Eἰ οὖν ταῦτα ἔλεγεν ὁ σωτὴρ καὶ μόνης τῆς ψυχῆς τὴν ζωὴν εὐηγγελίζετο, τί καινὸν ἡμῖν ἔφερε παρὰ Πυθαγόραν καὶ Πλάτωνα καὶ τὸν τούτων χορόν; Νῦν δὲ τὴν καινὴν καὶ ξένην εὐαγγελιζόμενος ἦλθεν ἀνθρώποις ἐλπίδα. Ξένον δὲ ἄρα ἦν καὶ καινὸν τὸ τὸν θεὸν ὑπισχνεῖσθαι μὴ τῇ ἀφθαρσίᾳ τὴν ἀφθαρσίαν τηρεῖν, ἀλλὰ τὴν φθορὰν ἀφθαρσίαν ποιεῖν. Ἀλλὰ γὰρ οὐκ ἄλλως λυμαίνεσθαι τὸν λόγον δυνάμενος ὁ τῆς πονηρίας ἄρχων ἐξέπεμψε τοὺς ἀποστόλους αὐτοῦ, κακὰς καὶ λοιμώδεις διδασκαλίας εἰσάγοντας, ἐκλεξάμενος αὐτοὺς ἐκ τῶν σταυρωσάντων τὸν σωτῆρα ἡμῶν, οἵτινες τὸ μὲν ὄνομα τοῦ σωτῆρος ἔφερον, τὰ δὲ ἔργα τοῦ πέμψαντος αὐτοὺς ἐποίουν, δι' οὓς καὶ τῷ ὀνόματι ἠκολούθησεν ἡ βλασφημία. Eἰ δὲ μὴ ἀνίσταται ἡ σάρξ, διὰ τί καὶ φυλάσσεται καὶ οὐ μᾶλλον αὐτῇ συγχωροῦμεν χρήσασθαι ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις, καὶ οὐ μιμούμεθα τοὺς ἰατρούς, οἵτινες, ἐπειδὰν ἀπεγνωσμένον ἔχωσιν ἄνθρωπον σώζεσθαι μὴ δυνάμενον, ἐπιτρέπουσιν αὐτῷ ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις ὑπηρετεῖν; Ἴσασι γὰρ ὅτι ἀπόλλυται. Ὅπερ ἀμέλει ποιοῦσιν οἱ τὴν σάρκα μισοῦντες, ἐκβάλλοντες αὐτὴν τῆς κληρονομίας, τὸ ὅσον ἐπ' αὐτοῖς· διὰ τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ ὡς νεκρὰν ἐσομένην ἀτιμάζουσιν αὐτήν. Eἰ δὲ ὁ ἡμέτερος ἰατρὸς Ἰησοῦς ὁ Χριστός, ἀπὸ τῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν ἡμῶν ἀποσπάσας, διαιτᾶται τῇ κατ' αὐτὸν σώφρονι καὶ ἐγκρατεῖ διαίτῃ τὴν σάρκα ἡμῶν, δῆλον ὡς ἐλπίδα σωτηρίας ἔχουσαν ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων αὐτὴν φυλάσσει, καθάπερ τοὺς ἐλπίδα σωτηρίας ἔχοντας ἀνθρώπους οἱ ἰατροὶ οὐκ ἐῶσιν ὑπηρετεῖν ταῖς ἡδοναῖς.
pass_a_gloss: There is a resurrection of the fallen body; for spirit does not fall. The soul is in the body, and the body, with the soul departing, is not. For the body is the house of the soul, and the soul is the house of the spirit. And these three things will be saved for those who have pure hope and unwavering faith in God. For even considering the worldly discourses, and not finding it impossible according to them for the body to have rebirth, and besides all these things, the Savior throughout the whole gospel shows the salvation of our body, why then do we tolerate the unbelieving and scandalous words, and do we forget ourselves, turning back, when we hear that the soul is immortal, but the body is perishable and no longer able to rise again? For we heard these things even before learning the truth from Pythagoras and Plato. If, then, the Savior said these things and preached the life of the soul alone, what new thing did he bring to us beyond Pythagoras and Plato and their followers? But now, preaching a new and strange hope to men, he came. And this was strange and new, that God promises not to keep immortality by immortality, but to make corruption immortality. But the ruler of wickedness, not being able to destroy the word in any other way, sent out his apostles, introducing evil and pestilential teachings, having chosen them from those who crucified our Savior, who bore the name of the Savior but did the deeds of the one who sent them, through whom also blasphemy followed the name. If the body does not rise, why is it also guarded, and should we not rather allow it to be used for desires, and not imitate the doctors, who, when they have a person who cannot be saved, permit him to serve desires? For they know that he is perishing. Which is what those who hate the body do, casting it out of the inheritance, as much as they can; for they also dishonor it as if it were going to be dead. But if our doctor, Jesus Christ, having torn us away from desires, diets our body with the sober and self-controlled diet according to him, it is clear that he guards it, having hope of salvation from sins, just as doctors do not permit people who have hope of salvation to serve pleasures.

choices.why: accurate translation of the perfect tense

pass_b_english: Resurrection belongs to the fallen body; spirit does not fall. The soul dwells in the body, yet it does not live in what is soulless; when the soul departs, the body ceases to be. The body is the soul's house, and the soul is the spirit's house. These three — body, soul, and spirit — will be saved for those who hold pure hope and unwavering faith in God.

Even if we weigh the world's own arguments, we find nothing in them that makes the body's rebirth impossible. On top of that, the Savior demonstrates the salvation of our flesh throughout the entire Gospel. So why do we still tolerate unbelieving, scandalous talk? Why do we forget ourselves and turn back when we hear that the soul is immortal while the body is perishable and supposedly unable to rise again? We heard that very claim long before we learned the truth from Pythagoras and Plato. If the Savior merely taught those things and proclaimed the soul's life alone, what new gift did he bring beyond Pythagoras, Plato, and their circle? But he came announcing a new and strange hope to humanity. And it was indeed strange and new: God promises not to preserve immortality by means of immortality, but to turn corruption into immortality.

Unable to destroy the Word in any other way, the ruler of wickedness dispatched his own apostles, choosing them from the very ones who crucified our Savior. They bore the Savior's name, yet they did the works of the one who sent them, and through them blasphemy clung to that name. They introduced evil, pestilential teachings.

If the body does not rise, why do we still guard it? Why not simply let it serve its desires? Why not imitate those physicians who, once they have a patient they cannot save, allow him to indulge his appetites? They know he is perishing. That is exactly what those who hate the body do: they cast it out of the inheritance, as far as they can, and they dishonor it as though it were already dead.

But our physician, Jesus Christ, has pulled us away from desires and puts our body on the sober, self‑controlled regimen that belongs to him. It is clear, then, that he guards the body because it carries the hope of salvation from sins — just as physicians do not permit patients who have hope of recovery to serve their pleasures.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, including the complex theological distinction regarding immortality and corruption (τὴν φθορὰν ἀφθαρσίαν ποιεῖν) and the comparison between the 'physicians' (ἰατρούς) of the world and Christ. Pass A preserves all clauses and the specific structure of the argument. Pass B provides a fluent rendering that maintains the agency and modality of the original.
